assertion.statement: For the actual B/F and every finite unramified Fprime/F, B0 has smooth geometrically connected residue fibre with surjective smooth reduction, and B(Fprime)/B0(Fprime) embeds in the fixed finite geometric component group, hence is killed by c_B.
assertion.objects: Actual fixed local elliptic curves B/F in the Heegner descent argument, B0 and Phi_B over the geometric residue field.
assertion.hypotheses: F is a nonarchimedean characteristic-zero local field and Fprime/F is finite unramified; the local curves range over the stated finite fixed list.
assertion.quantifiers: Every such local curve and unramified extension, including even extension degrees.
assertion.parameter_range: All residue characteristics; arbitrary reduction type.
assertion.uniformity: For each fixed B, the same geometric c_B; take a common multiple for the finite fixed list.
assertion.constants: c_B=order of Phi_B(kbar); no asserted numerical estimate.
assertion.normalizations: B0(Fprime) means integral points of the Neron identity open subgroup.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No assertion for arbitrary ramified base change; no cohomology vanishing supplied by this geometry-only input.
assertion.limit_order: Fix each local curve before forming c_B and varying the unramified extension.

use.reason: Supplies the actual geometric prerequisites for the existing Lang, formal-cohomology and fixed-local arguments without using their outgoing cohomological conclusions as premises.
use.shared_contract_justification: The three note paragraphs refer to the same B/F, Neron identity subgroup and unramified Fprime/F. The identical geometric input is used first for smooth Lang lifting, then the component quotient, then invariance of geometric component order.

adverse_cases.reason: The Lang theorem, additive normal-basis argument, formal-group filtration and limiting correction, and the resulting H1 annihilation are separate inputs or local deductions in the existing proof. No good-reduction assumption, semistability assumption, division by the extension degree, or bound uniform over arbitrary varying elliptic curves is asserted. CM point reduction, extension of a modular parametrization, and Atkin–Lehner actions are not supplied.
